proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(s,t\in\mathbb R\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\), which is a member condition of \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\), \(p_x>0\), so the conditional channels are defined.  From the definitions of the replicates,
\[
 e^{i(sS_1+tS_2)}=e^{i(s+t)A}e^{isU_1}e^{itU_2}.
\]
The joint independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}latent\text{-}independence}\) and the coordinate independence in \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}coordinate\text{-}independence}\) therefore give
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_x(s,t)
&=E_P[e^{i(s+t)A}\mid X=x]E_P[e^{isU_1}]E_P[e^{itU_2}]\\
&=\left\{\int_{\mathcal A}e^{i(s+t)a}f_x(a)\,da\right\}\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\\
&=\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
The same two independence assumptions allow the bounded mark to remain with the latent variables.  Thus, using the definitions of \(m_x\) and \(q_x\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_x(s,t)
&=E_P[Ye^{i(s+t)A}\mid X=x]E_P[e^{isU_1}]E_P[e^{itU_2}]\\
&=\left\{\int_{\mathcal A}e^{i(s+t)a}E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]f_x(a)\,da\right\}\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\\
&=\widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
All expectations are finite: the probability-channel integrands have modulus one, while \(|Y|\le B_Y\) follows from consistency and bounded potential outcomes, both member conditions of \(\mathcal M\).  This proves both identities.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Positivity of \(p_x\) from \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) makes \(F_x\) and \(G_x\) functionals of the observed conditional law.  Put
\[
 \delta=\min\left\{\frac{\nu_0}{2},\frac{1}{4B_A}\right\}>0.
\]
For \(|v|\le2\delta\), compact support of \(A\) and \(|e^{iz}-1|\le |z|\) imply
\[
 |\widehat f_x(v)-1|
 \le \int_{\mathcal A}|e^{iva}-1|f_x(a)\,da
 \le B_A|v|\le\frac12.
\]
Consequently \(|\widehat f_x(v)|\ge1/2\) there.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}local\text{-}modulus}\) also gives \(|\phi_j(v)|\ge c_0\) for \(|v|\le2\delta\).  The factorization lemma therefore shows that \(F_x(u,t)\ne0\) whenever \(|u|,|t|\le\delta\).

Since \(A\) is bounded and \(E_P|U_2|<\infty\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}moment}\), dominated differentiation is valid.  Dividing the derivative of the first factorization identity by its nonzero value yields, for \(|u|\le\delta\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_x(u)
&:=\frac{\left.\partial_tF_x(u,t)\right|_{t=0}}{F_x(u,0)}\\
&=\frac{\widehat f_x'(u)}{\widehat f_x(u)}+\frac{\phi_2'(0)}{\phi_2(0)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every quantity defining \(D_x\) is observed.  Characteristic-function normalization gives \(\phi_2(0)=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}center\text{-}two}\) gives
\[
 \phi_2'(0)=iE_P[U_2]=0.
\]
Hence
\[
 \widehat f_x'(u)=D_x(u)\widehat f_x(u),\qquad \widehat f_x(0)=1.
\]
If two laws in \(\mathcal M\) have the same observed law, their functions \(D_x\) coincide.  For the ratio \(R(u)=\widehat f_x^{(1)}(u)/\widehat f_x^{(0)}(u)\) on \([-\delta,\delta]\), the preceding differential equation gives \(R'(u)=0\) and \(R(0)=1\).  Thus the two latent transforms agree on this interval.  Notice that no derivative of \(\phi_1\), and hence no location normalization on \(U_1\), entered this argument.

By \(\mathrm{ass{:}compact\text{-}dose}\), for every complex \(z\),
\[
 |e^{iza}f_x(a)|\le e^{B_A|\operatorname{Im}z|}f_x(a),
\]
so dominated differentiation of every order makes \(\widehat f_x\) entire.  For the difference \(H\) of two candidate transforms, \(H(u)=0\) for real \(|u|<\delta\).  Every real derivative of \(H\) at zero is consequently zero; complex differentiability makes these the complex derivatives, and the everywhere-convergent Taylor expansion
\[
 H(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{H^{(k)}(0)}{k!}z^k
\]
is therefore identically zero.  Thus local equality extends to all of \(\mathbb C\) without requiring either error transform to be nonzero outside the protected neighborhood.

For the marked channel, the two factorizations at \((u,0)\), together with \(F_x(u,0)\ne0\), give the observed local formula
\[
 \widehat q_x(u)=\widehat f_x(u)\frac{G_x(u,0)}{F_x(u,0)},\qquad |u|\le\delta.
\]
Bounded outcomes imply \(|q_x|\le B_Yf_x\) almost everywhere, so \(q_x\) is integrable and supported on \(\mathcal A\).  The same dominated-differentiation argument makes \(\widehat q_x\) entire, and the same Taylor-series argument extends its locally recovered value globally.

It remains only to check that equality of these transforms identifies the functions rather than merely their transforms.  If \(h\) is the difference of two candidate \(f_x\)'s, or of two candidate \(q_x\)'s, then \(h\in L^1(\mathbb R)\), is supported on \(\mathcal A\), and its Fourier transform vanishes on all of \(\mathbb R\).  Let
\[
 g_\epsilon(v)=(2\pi\epsilon)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/(2\epsilon)}.
\]
The elementary Gaussian integral gives
\[
 g_\epsilon(v)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-itv}e^{-\epsilon t^2/2}\,dt.
\]
Fubini's theorem is applicable because \(h\in L^1\) and the Gaussian multiplier is integrable, and hence
\[
 (h*g_\epsilon)(a)
 =\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-ita}\widehat h(t)e^{-\epsilon t^2/2}\,dt=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \|h*g_\epsilon-h\|_1
 \le\int_{\mathbb R}g_\epsilon(v)\|h(\cdot-v)-h\|_1\,dv\longrightarrow0.
\]
The last limit follows by first checking translation continuity for compactly supported step functions and then approximating \(h\) in \(L^1\).  Thus \(h=0\) almost everywhere.  Finally, \(\beta>1/2\) gives unique continuous Sobolev representatives: this follows from Cauchy--Schwarz because \(\int(1+t^2)^{-\beta}\,dt<\infty\).  Those representatives therefore agree everywhere.  Hence the observed law uniquely determines every density \(f_x\) and every outcome-weighted density \(q_x\), including when an error characteristic function vanishes on an open set away from zero.

Let \(m=|\mathcal X|\) and
\[
 \epsilon_n=\left\{\frac{\log(6m/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
For each \(x\), \(\widehat p_x\) is the average of \(n\) independent Bernoulli variables, by \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\).  If \(Z\in[0,1]\), exponential tilting and two differentiations of the log moment-generating function give
\[
 \log E[e^{\lambda(Z-EZ)}]\le\frac{\lambda^2}{8},\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R.
\]
Indeed, the second derivative is the variance of a tilted variable in \([0,1]\), which is at most \(1/4\), while the value and first derivative at zero are zero.  Exponential Markov, independence, and optimization at \(\lambda=4\epsilon_n\) for the upper tail and \(\lambda=-4\epsilon_n\) for the lower tail therefore give
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(|\widehat p_x-p_x|>\epsilon_n)
 \le2e^{-2n\epsilon_n^2}=\frac{\alpha}{3m}.
\]
The union bound over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) therefore gives
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\left(\max_x|\widehat p_x-p_x|\le\epsilon_n\right)\ge1-\frac\alpha3.
\]
Because the true mass vector is nonnegative and sums to one, the event in parentheses is exactly its membership in \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), by \(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\).  The displayed coordinate bound is part of the same definition.

For the count claim, if \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p)\), exponential Markov applied to \(e^{-tN}\), followed by \(1-p+pe^{-t}\le\exp\{p(e^{-t}-1)\}\), gives
\[
 P(N\le np/2)\le\inf_{t>0}\exp\{tnp/2+np(e^{-t}-1)\}.
\]
Choosing \(t=\log2\) makes the exponent \(-np(1-\log2)/2\le-np/8\).  Therefore, for \(n_x\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n,p_x)\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(n_x<np_x/2)\le e^{-np_x/8}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) has \(p_x\ge p_{\min}\), so another union bound yields
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}\left(\min_xn_x<np_{\min}/2\right)
 \le\sum_xe^{-np_x/8}
 \le m e^{-np_{\min}/8}.
\]

Finally, let \(p\) and \(p'\) be two mass vectors in the confidence region while \((f_x,q_x)\) is fixed and feasible.  Feasibility in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\), or bounded outcomes for a model member, gives \(|q_x(a)/f_x(a)|\le B_Y\) wherever the quotient is used.  Hence, uniformly over \(a\in I\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|\sum_x(p_x-p_x')\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
&\le B_Y\sum_x|p_x-p_x'|\\
&\le2B_Ym\epsilon_n.
\end{aligned}
\]
Writing \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>1\),
\[
 \frac{\epsilon_n}{r_n}
 =O\left(n^{-1/2}\left\{\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right\}^{\gamma}\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
This proves the claimed profiling contribution and all three probability bounds.

Assume the affirmative content posed by \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\), and abbreviate
\[
 Q_{j,n}=((P_{j,n})_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n},\qquad
 \Delta_n=\|\mu_{1,n}-\mu_{0,n}\|_{L^\infty(I)}.
\]
Fix an arbitrary \(\mathcal C_n=(L_n,U_n)\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and define its simultaneous coverage events
\[
 H_{j,n}=\{L_n(a)\le\mu_{j,n}(a)\le U_n(a)\text{ for every }a\in I\}.
\]
Because both alternatives belong to \(\mathcal M\), honesty gives \(Q_{j,n}(H_{j,n})\ge1-\alpha\).  The total-variation inequality and the assumed bound \(\operatorname{TV}(Q_{0,n},Q_{1,n})\le\eta\) imply
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{1,n})\ge Q_{1,n}(H_{1,n})-\eta\ge1-\alpha-\eta.
\]
Consequently
\[
 Q_{0,n}(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n})\ge1-2\alpha-\eta>0.
\]
On \(H_{0,n}\cap H_{1,n}\), the interval \([L_n(a),U_n(a)]\) contains both \(\mu_{0,n}(a)\) and \(\mu_{1,n}(a)\) for every \(a\), and hence
\[
 W_n\ge\Delta_n.
\]
Since \(W_n\ge0\) by \(\mathrm{def{:}honest\text{-}bands}\),
\[
 E_{Q_{0,n}}[W_n]
 \ge(1-2\alpha-\eta)\Delta_n
 \ge(1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}K_n^{1/2-\beta}.
\]
This inequality holds for every honest band, and its left side is bounded above by \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}W_n\).  Taking the infimum over \(\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\) proves the minimax assertion with \(c'=(1-2\alpha-\eta)c_{\mathrm{sep}}>0\).  Finally, if \(\gamma=\beta-1/2\), then for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \frac12\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\le K_n\le\frac{\log n}{\log\log n},
\]
so \(K_n^{-\gamma}\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^\gamma=r_n\), completing the claimed comparison.

Suppose \(Y(a)=1\) almost surely for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).  Consistency gives \(Y=1\) almost surely, and therefore \(m_x(a)=1\) for the conditional-regression version on the support of \(f_x\).  Hence
\[
 q_x(a)=m_x(a)f_x(a)=f_x(a).
\]
The two definitions of the observable channels now give, for all \(s,t\),
\[
 G_x(s,t)=E[Ye^{i(sS_1+tS_2)}\mid X=x]
 =E[e^{i(sS_1+tS_2)}\mid X=x]=F_x(s,t),
\]
and the causal definition gives \(\mu(a)=E[Y(a)]=1\).

The cited \(\mathrm{lem{:}capitao\text{-}theorem\text{-}one}\) applies to the probability channel: compact support of \(A\) implies its condition (H2), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}error\text{-}coordinate\text{-}independence}\) is its condition (H1).  That theorem identifies the latent and error laws up to their common translation.  In the present scalar model, \(E_P[U_2]=0\) fixes this translation, exactly as the derivative calculation in \(\mathrm{thm{:}marked\text{-}cocycle\text{-}id}\) shows.  Thus, after deleting the now redundant marked channel \(G_x=F_x\), the probability-channel argument is the stated normalized special case of their Theorem 1.

added_lemmas.statement: Theorem 1 of Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Leh\'ericy states that in their two-replicate additive model, condition (H2) for each latent signal and coordinate independence (H1) for each error law make equality of observed convolution laws identify both the latent-signal law and the error law up to translation.

attestation.note: Verified against Theorem 1 in the published article; the node paraphrases its H1--H2 assumptions and conclusion.

added_lemmas.statement: Low's two-point expected-length argument lower-bounds the expected length of a confidence interval having prescribed uniform coverage by combining parameter separation with the testing affinity of two data laws.

attestation.note: Verified against the published article's stated expected-length inequality and Proposition 1; the exact band specialization is derived in this note.

proposed_assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(X\), the random potential-outcome process is independent of treatment: \(\sigma\{Y(a):a\in\mathcal A\}\perp A\mid X\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: Coordinatewise weak unconfoundedness does not control the treatment-dependent diagonal of an uncountable potential-outcome process. The spike-schedule witness in the ADRF obligation satisfies every frozen coordinatewise independence statement but is excluded by full-process conditional independence. This strengthening remains compatible with Bernoulli potential outcomes generated from an independent common uniform variable.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is a standard causal exchangeability refinement; it does not assume analytic measurement-error identification, a stability modulus, a rate, or the lower construction.

proposed_assumptions.condition: For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the map \(a\mapsto E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]\) is continuous on \(I\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: Process independence and almost-sure consistency identify the latent regression only almost everywhere in dose. Continuity of the stratum-specific causal mean, together with continuity of the Sobolev regression and the density lower bound, extends that equality to every target dose required by a simultaneous band.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This regularity condition only selects the pointwise version after an almost-everywhere causal equality; it does not posit the identifying formula or any inference conclusion.

proposed.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every \(x\in\mathcal X\), and all real \(s,t\), \(F_x(s,t)=\widehat f_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\) and \(G_x(s,t)=\widehat q_x(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t)\).
proposed.justification: This is the observable two-channel factorization on which injectivity and inference rest.
proposed.gap: Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy analyze only the first identity; the marked identity is absent from their model.
proposed.consumer: The empirical characteristic-function confidence set uses these residual equations jointly.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses positive cell mass to define the conditional channels, compact support for the displayed integrals, and bounded observed outcomes for the marked expectation; these model conditions must be explicit dependencies.

proposed.statement: Conditional on an affirmative resolution of \(\mathrm{oeq{:}fixed\text{-}nuisance\text{-}marked\text{-}modulus}\), Low's two-point expected-length inequality gives constants \(c'>0\) and \(n_1\) such that \(\inf_{\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\ge c'K_n^{1/2-\beta}\asymp c'r_n\) for every \(n\ge n_1\); positivity of \(c'\) follows from \(\eta<1-2\alpha\).
proposed.justification: This is deliberately a conditional corollary: the generic testing reduction is routine once the marked modulus has been constructed.
proposed.gap: No cited ADRF or blind repeated-measurement paper gives a converse quantifying over every honest measurable band.
proposed.consumer: Together with the upper theorem, it gives the irreducible resolution of a two-recall ADRF curve.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The statement explicitly attributes its testing reduction to Low's published expected-length inequality, so the cited theorem-level leaf is added to the dependency list.

proposed.statement: The map \(P\mapsto P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is injective for \(\{(f_x,q_x):x\in\mathcal X\}\) over \(\mathcal M\). On a common neighborhood of zero, \(\left.\partial_t\log F_x(u,t)\right|_{t=0}=\widehat f_x'(u)/\widehat f_x(u)+\phi_2'(0)=\widehat f_x'(u)/\widehat f_x(u)\), because \(\phi_2(0)=1\) and \(\phi_2'(0)=iE_P[U_2]=0\). Together with \(\widehat f_x(0)=1\), this derivative identity uniquely fixes the latent translation without a normalization on \(U_1\). Moreover, \(\widehat q_x(u)=\widehat f_x(u)G_x(u,0)/F_x(u,0)\). Compact support makes both recovered transforms entire, so the local formulas determine \(f_x\) and \(q_x\) globally even when either error transform has an open zero set away from zero.
proposed.justification: It makes the causal ratio a functional of the observed marked replicate law without symmetry or global nonvanishing.
proposed.gap: Theorem 1 of Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy gives the probability-channel cocycle; it does not state the outcome-weighted signed channel or its compatibility with the recovered probability channel.
proposed.consumer: It supplies the law-level target set for honest-band inversion in two-recall exposure studies.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Differentiation uses the error moment and marked-transform integrability uses bounded outcomes; these proof dependencies were implicit through model membership and are made direct.

proposed.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha/3\). On this event, \(\max_x|p_x-\widehat p_x|\le[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\); moreover \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\min_xn_x<np_{\min}/2)\le|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\). For fixed feasible \(f_x,q_x\), mass profiling adds at most \(2B_Y|\mathcal X|[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}=o(r_n)\) to the ADRF diameter.
proposed.justification: The empirical cell masses are random inputs to the causal mixture and must enter the same simultaneous coverage event as the two transform channels.
proposed.gap: The blind-deconvolution comparators do not profile finite-stratum causal weights jointly with probability and marked transform restrictions.
proposed.consumer: The bound adds cell-count uncertainty to coverage while showing that its diameter contribution is negligible relative to the analytic inverse rate.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The count bound uses stratum positivity, and the profiling bound uses the feasible domination condition or bounded outcomes; these proof dependencies were absent from the frozen edge list.

proposed.statement: In the standard special case \(Y(a)=1\) almost surely for every \(a\), one has \(q_x=f_x\), \(G_x=F_x\), and \(\mu(a)=1\); the probability-channel part of \(\mathrm{thm{:}marked\text{-}cocycle\text{-}id}\), with location normalized only by \(E_P[U_2]=0\), reduces to Theorem 1 of Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Leh\'ericy.
proposed.justification: The reduction checks that the marked construction preserves the established unmarked model.
proposed.gap: This is a compatibility result rather than a novelty claim.
proposed.consumer: It allows implementations to reuse the existing unmarked analytic-sieve path when the mark carries no information.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparison invokes the published Theorem 1 and must depend on its cited leaf. The ADRF theorem is unnecessary because the special-case causal mean equals one directly from the hypothesis.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The pointwise causal equality over all of \(I\) is not implied by the frozen weak-unconfoundedness and almost-sure-consistency conditions.
open_obligations.obstruction: Conditioning at \(A=a\) is a null-event version choice. A diagonal spike potential-outcome schedule gives the same observed regression and satisfies the two frozen causal assumptions but changes \(E[Y(a)]\) at every fixed dose. Thus the target is false on the current class, not merely unproved.
open_obligations.attempted: The standard g-formula derivation was audited at the regular-conditional-distribution step. Continuity of \(q_x/f_x\) alone cannot repair an unrestricted treatment-dependent diagonal. Full-process conditional independence and causal-mean continuity are proposed because together they derive, rather than assume, the pointwise bridge and remain compatible with the Bernoulli lower experiment.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The analytic part is complete: \(p_x\), \(f_x\), and \(q_x\) are observed-law functionals and \(f_x\ge\kappa\) on \(I\), so
\[
 \mu^{\mathrm{reg}}(a):=\sum_xp_x\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
\]
is an identified continuous curve.  Under the two proposed causal regularity conditions, put \(g_x(a)=E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]\).  Full-process conditional independence and consistency give \(m_x(a)=g_x(a)\) for \(f_x(a)\,da\)-almost every \(a\): the conditional law of the whole response process given \((A,X)\) equals its law given \(X\), and evaluation at the realized coordinate is \(Y=Y(A)\).  The proposed condition makes \(g_x\) continuous, while \(m_x=q_x/f_x\) is continuous on \(I\) because \(\beta>3/2\) and \(f_x\ge\kappa\).  Since \(f_x\ge\kappa\), equality almost everywhere is Lebesgue equality almost everywhere, and continuity extends it to every \(a\in I\).  The causal calculation is then equation-by-equation:
\[
 E_P[Y(a)]=\sum_xp_xE_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]
 =\sum_xp_xm_x(a)=\sum_xp_x\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}.
\]
The current assumptions alone do not justify the middle equality at point doses.  Indeed, start from any admissible nuisance law and choose \(c>0\) small enough that \(c\le B_Y\) and \(\|cf_x\|_{H^\beta}\le R_q\) in every cell.  One full-data extension can set \(Y_0(a)=c\) for all \(a\); another can set \(Y_1(a)=c\mathbf 1\{A=a\}\).  Under a continuously distributed \(A\), for every fixed \(a\), \(Y_1(a)=0\) almost surely and is therefore independent of \(A\) given \(X\), while consistency gives \(Y_1=Y_1(A)=c\).  Both extensions have the same observed law and the same \(m_x=c\) and \(q_x=cf_x\), but their causal curves are respectively \(c\) and zero.  This is an explicit diagonal-null-set witness.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construction of the fixed-nuisance Bernoulli packet and its product-experiment total-variation bound remains open after the analytic attenuation calculation.
open_obligations.obstruction: The declared index ranges do not even ensure a nonempty strict-interior lower submodel: they omit \(\kappa|I|\le1\), the necessary Sobolev-radius lower bound, and an interior spectral restriction excluding \(c_0=1\) for asymmetric errors. Under compatible indices, the missing mathematical step is a weighted chi-square or Hellinger bound for the two-replicate baseline together with a packet satisfying all range and Sobolev constraints.
open_obligations.attempted: I carried the moment-annihilation packet through the exact marked-channel Fourier factorization and obtained factorial low-frequency attenuation. I also tested the frozen index endpoints and found explicit feasibility obstructions before the total-variation conversion.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Two necessary compatibility checks follow from the frozen assumptions.  Every candidate fixed density must satisfy
\[
 1=\int_{\mathcal A}f_x(a)\,da\ge\int_I f_x(a)\,da\ge\kappa |I|
\]
and, by Cauchy--Schwarz and \(|\mathcal A|=2B_A\),
\[
 R_f\ge\|f_x\|_{H^\beta}\ge\|f_x\|_2\ge(2B_A)^{-1/2}.
\]
Neither restriction is imposed on the declared index ranges.  There is also an error-law obstruction at the allowed endpoint \(c_0=1\): if a characteristic function obeys \(|\phi(t)|=1\) on a nondegenerate interval, equality in \(|E e^{itU}|\le1\), at two noncommensurate nonzero frequencies, forces \(U\) to be almost surely constant.  Thus the required asymmetric compact-spectrum errors cannot exist at that endpoint.

Conditional on compatible fixed nuisances, the proposed polynomial-packet route does have the required analytic attenuation.  If \(h_n=f(b_{1,n}-b_{0,n})\) annihilates all polynomials of degree below \(K_n\), then for \(|u|\le\Omega\), Taylor's formula gives
\[
 |\widehat h_n(u)|
 \le \|h_n\|_1 e^{B_A\Omega}\frac{(B_A\Omega)^{K_n}}{K_n!}.
\]
For errors whose transforms are supported in fixed intervals, the two-dimensional Fourier transform of the marked observed-density perturbation is exactly
\[
 \widehat h_n(s+t)\phi_1(s)\phi_2(t),
\]
so it is confined to a fixed square and has the same factorial attenuation.  What remains is to construct the packet with the simultaneous \(H^\beta\), Bernoulli-range, and \(L^\infty(I)\) calibrations and to convert this Fourier bound into a uniform product-experiment total-variation bound through a proved lower envelope for the baseline observed density.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The constrained-sieve embedding and the quantitative discrete analytic-cocycle modulus at order \(K_n^{1/2-\beta}\) are not established.
open_obligations.obstruction: Local qualitative identifiability gives no uniform singular-value estimate. The frozen core supplies neither a proved stability inequality for the bilinear grid map nor a specified shape-preserving Jackson construction satisfying every sieve constraint.
open_obligations.attempted: I proved the simultaneous empirical-transform event with the stated radii and the global clipping bound, then isolated the remaining deterministic inverse inequality. Direct interpolation is insufficient because it does not control the unknown error factors or preserve the nonlinear quotient constraints.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The confidence-event and clipping portions are derivable.  Conditional on \(n_x\), each complex probability summand has modulus at most one and each marked summand has modulus at most \(B_Y\).  Applying the real bounded-variable exponential inequality to real and imaginary parts gives, when \(n_x>\lambda_n\),
\[
 P\left(\left.|\widehat F_{x,n}-F_x|>2\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\,\right|\,(X_i)_{i=1}^n\right)\le4e^{-\lambda_n},
\]
and the analogous bound for \(G_x\) with radius \(2B_Y\sqrt{\lambda_n/n_x}\).  When \(n_x\le\lambda_n\), the deterministic bounds \(|\widehat F-F|\le2\) and \(|\widehat G-G|\le2B_Y\) apply.  A union bound over both channels, all cells, and \(\mathcal D_n\) costs at most \(8|\mathcal X||\mathcal D_n|e^{-\lambda_n}=\alpha/6\).  Together with \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\), this proves \(P(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha/2\), hence the weaker claimed \(1-\alpha\) bound.  Also, every feasible \(\mu_\theta\) lies in \([-B_Y,B_Y]\); the endpoint definition therefore gives \(0\le W_n\le2B_Y\), including the empty-set convention.

The unproved kernel is the uniform quantitative inverse estimate
\[
 \sup_{\theta,\theta'\in\Theta_{n,\alpha}}
 \|\mu_\theta-\mu_{\theta'}\|_{L^\infty(I)}
 \lesssim K_n^{1/2-\beta}+\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}.
\]
Qualitative analytic continuation does not imply this modulus.  A proof must give singular-value bounds for the discrete bilinear cocycle with two unknown atomic error factors and then transfer them through the quotient.  In addition, no shape-preserving Jackson operator has been specified that simultaneously preserves normalization, the lower bound on \(I\), the \(H^\beta\) radii, and \(|q|\le B_Yf\); ordinary Jackson approximation alone establishes none of those feasibility constraints.

open_obligations.partial_result:
If the unresolved embedding and deterministic stability assertions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) hold and the pointwise causal bridge is added, the remainder of the upper theorem is complete.  On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), a feasible approximating tuple \(\bar\theta\) with \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta}-\mu\|_\infty\le b_{\mu,n}\) implies \(L_n\le\mu\le U_n\) pointwise by the endpoint definitions.  On the regular-count event, deterministic feasible-set diameter plus the two endpoint inflations is \(O(r_n)\), since \(b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{1/2-\beta})\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}=o(r_n)\).  On count failure, clipping gives \(W_n\le2B_Y\), while \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) gives probability at most \(|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\).  Therefore
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_PW_n
 \le Cr_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}
 =O(r_n).
\]
Thus no additional probabilistic argument is missing; the analytic inverse modulus, feasible embedding, and pointwise causal bridge are the exact blockers.
